preamble: /d/ becomes voiceless [θ] by spirantization plus devoicing at the end of a word or before a voiceless consonant. In Madrid and its surroundings, colloquial speech realizes word-final /d/ as [θ] (Madrid [maˈðɾiθ], sed [seθ]) alongside standard [ð̥] or zero. Gothic shows the same outcome as a regular rule: after a vowel, /d/ was devoiced to þ [θ] word-finally and before a voiceless consonant, giving alternations such as gōþs 'good' beside genitive gōdis and haubiþ 'head' beside haubidis.

examples.note: Colloquial realization of word-final /d/ as [θ] in Madrid and its surroundings, alongside standard [ð̥] or zero.
Same word-final realization; nonstandard outside central Spain.
After a vowel and before a voiceless consonant or word end, /d/ was devoiced to þ [θ]; the stem keeps d before a vowel.

examples.from: haubidis 'of the head' (genitive), stem haubid- (< Proto-Germanic *haubudą)
examples.note: Word-final /d/ devoiced to þ, alternating with d in the inflected forms.
